title: Hyundai Mobis Signs Deal to Sell Lamp Business to France's OP Mobility
content:
Korea Supply Chain Brief · September 30, 2026

Hyundai Mobis has signed a definitive Stock Purchase Agreement to sell its lamp (lighting) business to French auto parts maker OP Mobility, after its board approved spinning the division off into a separate legal entity first. Here is what was disclosed and why Hyundai Mobis is calling this a "selection and concentration" move.

CompanyRoleEvidence
Hyundai Mobis
KRX: 012330		Spinning off and selling its lamp business divisionFiling (board resolution and SPA disclosed Sep 30, 2026)
OP Mobility (France)Buyer of the spun-off lamp business entityFiling

What was disclosed

  • Board action: Hyundai Mobis held an extraordinary board meeting on September 30 and approved a spin-off (physical division) of its lamp business unit into a standalone legal entity.
  • Deal: The same day, Hyundai Mobis signed a Stock Purchase Agreement (SPA) with OP Mobility to sell that spun-off entity once it is formed.
  • Timeline: The company set a target spin-off date of April 1, 2027, after which the newly formed lamp business entity would be sold to OP Mobility.
  • Employees: Staff assigned to the transferred division keep their employment and all related rights and obligations carry over to the new entity unchanged.
  • Remaining steps: Shareholder meeting approval and merger control filings are still to come before the transaction closes.

Why Hyundai Mobis is selling a core parts business

The company frames this as part of a "selection and concentration" strategy: freeing up management resources and capital from the lamp business so headquarters can focus on new growth areas and core businesses tied to the shift toward future mobility. Hyundai Mobis argues the lamp business itself benefits too, gaining an independent management structure and, through combination with OP Mobility, stronger global competitiveness as a standalone lighting specialist rather than a division inside a larger parts supplier.

How this deal came together

The sale builds on a preliminary memorandum of understanding (MOU) the two companies signed in January 2026, which first laid out the "selection and concentration" rationale and OP Mobility as the intended buyer. Since then, the two sides negotiated deal structure and separation details, with Hyundai Mobis reported to have kept internal staff updated on progress throughout. The SPA signed September 30 converts that MOU into a binding agreement, though the transaction is not yet closed.

What is not disclosed

  • The sale price or other financial terms of the SPA.
  • The lamp business division's current revenue or headcount.
  • A specific date for the shareholder vote or expected merger-control clearance timeline.

Quick FAQ

Has the lamp business sale actually closed?
No. Hyundai Mobis has signed a binding Stock Purchase Agreement and its board approved the spin-off, but shareholder approval and merger control filings are still pending, and the spin-off itself is targeted for April 1, 2027.

Who is OP Mobility?
OP Mobility is a French automotive parts company; the report identifies it as the buyer of Hyundai Mobis's spun-off lamp business entity under the SPA.

What happens to employees in the lamp business?
Employees assigned to the division keep their jobs, with their employment rights and obligations carrying over to the new entity as part of the spin-off.
